narration: A beautiful screen is only the top layer of an app. Underneath it are four more layers deciding what actually happens.
onScreenText: The screen is only layer one.
voiceDirection: Warm, clear and visual. Read calmly, with emphasis on 'top layer' and 'four more layers'.

narration: Layer one is the interface: buttons, forms, screens and feedback. It is what the user sees and touches.
captionText: What the user sees and touches.
voiceDirection: Keep it simple and concrete. Slight emphasis on 'sees and touches'.

narration: Layer two is application logic. It decides what a click means, which rules run, and what should happen next.
voiceDirection: Conversational, slightly rhythmic on the three actions.

narration: Layer three is the API or backend. It receives requests, validates them, and coordinates work between the app and other systems.
Layer four is data and identity: your database, authentication and permissions. This is where information and access rules live.
voiceDirection: Steady and reassuring. Do not make the security point sound alarming.

narration: Layer five is infrastructure and deployment: the environment that keeps the app running, configured, reachable and observable.
voiceDirection: Keep this accessible. Pronounce 'observable' naturally, without sounding overly technical.

narration: Now watch a login travel down the stack: interface, logic, backend, identity and data. The result then travels back up to the user.
voiceDirection: Slightly faster and more animated to match the travelling request.

narration: When something breaks, ask which layer owns the problem. That one question makes AI-built apps much easier to debug.
captionText: Find the layer that owns the problem.
voiceDirection: Finish confidently and cleanly. Emphasize 'which layer owns the problem'.
